agent_notes: This diff is a net security improvement: it closes a prior gap where InstanceConfig.url loaded from triggarr.toml had no SSRF-style validation at all (only the apikey= rejection existed). No exploitable defect was identified in the new field_validator wiring itself; validate_arr_url_config() (triggarr/web/validation.py, not modified in this diff) was reviewed for context and its intentional relaxations (permitting loopback/localhost) match its docstring's stated D-01/D-02 rationale.

Verified the web settings form path (triggarr/web/routes.py save_settings) applies the stricter validate_arr_url() (which blocks loopback) before model construction, so the relaxed config-load validator does not weaken web-submitted input — it only widens what is accepted when editing triggarr.toml directly on disk.

findings.problem: This hunk wires `validate_arr_url_config()` into `InstanceConfig.url` as the only SSRF check applied to config-file-sourced URLs (previously none existed on this path). That underlying function (triggarr/web/validation.py, unchanged by this diff) explicitly accepts unresolved hostnames without DNS resolution and compares against a small exact-string `BLOCKED_HOSTS` set, so DNS rebinding and non-canonical hostname forms (e.g. a trailing dot) are acknowledged residual risks in its own docstring. The diff is a net tightening (closes a previously-open gap), but it now makes this specific function's coverage load-bearing at every config load, including for disabled instances.
findings.title: Config-load SSRF validator becomes sole enforcement point with documented residual bypasses
findings.why_it_matters: If a bypass input exists (e.g. a hostname variant that evades the exact-match BLOCKED_HOSTS check, or DNS rebinding against an allowed hostname), outbound *arr client requests could still reach cloud metadata or other blocked targets. No such bypass is demonstrated here; this is a note about increased reliance on an already-documented-limited validator, not a defect introduced by this hunk.

agent_notes: No import cycle was introduced. triggarr/web/validation.py imports only __future__, ipaddress, re and urllib.parse, and triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty, so importing it from models does not load fastapi or routes.

The new validator follows the existing pattern: InstanceConfig already uses an @field_validator('url') (reject_apikey_in_url, line 65) that raises ValueError so Pydantic reports a ValidationError. The new validator uses the same mechanism.

Two URL validators now coexist on purpose: validate_arr_url (strict, used by web/routes.py at save time) and validate_arr_url_config (relaxed, allows loopback, used at config load). This split looks deliberate per the D-01/D-02 references in the docstring and commit 14eecb5, so it is not flagged as a pattern inconsistency. Someone should confirm that routes still runs the strict check on save, so a loopback URL accepted at load cannot be saved through the UI unless that is intended.

Pydantic runs the two url validators in the order they are defined (apikey check, then SSRF check). They are independent, so the order does not matter, but a URL with apikey= reports the apikey error first.

The docstring says the validator rejects disabled instances with unsafe URLs at startup. That is a behavior and blast-radius question for existing user configs, covered by the impact agent, not an architecture finding.

Function-local imports of web code from non-web code already appear in triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532 and :538, so the import style matches the codebase. Those cases also cross the same layer boundary.

findings.problem: InstanceConfig in triggarr/models/config.py is imported by the core layers (config.py, db.py, state.py, startup.py, search/engine.py, search/scheduler.py). findings.title: Domain model layer now depends on the web package for URL validation

If someone later adds a fastapi or models import to web/validation.py or web/__init__.py, loading the config pulls in the web stack or creates a real import cycle, and the function-local import hides that risk.

agent_notes: Blast radius: InstanceConfig is imported by 9 production modules and 17 test files, but the public API is unchanged. Only a new field_validator was added, and the url field's type and default ('') are the same. No signatures changed and no schema or DB migration is needed. The validator only checks the value; it does not change it.

Validator order: Pydantic runs both @field_validator('url') methods in definition order (reject_apikey_in_url, then validate_url_ssrf). Both only raise and return the value unchanged, so the order does not affect behaviour.

Construction paths affected: startup load (config.py ensure_config -> load_settings), settings POST (routes.py:597 SettingsModel(**new_config), wrapped in except ValidationError -> redirect), add_instance (routes.py:790, url='' is accepted by the empty-URL shortcut), and the in-request reloads at routes.py:1199/1462/1511/1535, which re-read TOML that was just written from an already-validated model and so should not newly fail.

Interaction with the web form: the settings POST already applies the stricter validate_arr_url (which blocks loopback) to edited instances. Untouched instances are preserved through the else-branch and now pass only through the relaxed validator, so existing localhost instances still save. Behaviour stays consistent: the UI rejects loopback for new input, and the config load accepts it.

Tailscale/CGNAT check (relevant to this owner's NAS setup): plain 100.x.y.z Tailscale IPv4 literals are allowed. Only the exact 100.100.100.200 and the IPv4-mapped IPv6 form within 100.64.0.0/10 are blocked. Existing Tailscale-addressed instances will not break.
Scheme-less URLs such as '192.168.1.5:7878' or 'radarr:7878' are now rejected at load. These never worked as an httpx base_url, so this is outside the input contract and not a regression.
Performance: the function-local import is served from the sys.modules cache after the first call. Validation is O(1) per instance with at most 5 instances per app type, so the cost is negligible.
Tests: the full suite passes (982 passed) with this diff applied.

Verdict: shippable as-is. The change tightens validation as intended. The only upgrade risk is that hand-edited TOML with unspecified, link-local or metadata URLs now aborts startup with a raw traceback. A friendly ValidationError exit in ensure_config would be a worthwhile follow-up.

findings.fix_hint: Consider catching pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config and exiting with a friendly loguru.error that names the field (as is already done for TOMLDecodeError), and add a changelog/upgrade note that hand-edited unsafe URLs now block startup.
findings.problem: validate_url_ssrf runs on every InstanceConfig construction, including the startup load via ensure_config -> load_settings (triggarr/config.py:371), and it runs even for disabled instances. Before this diff, a hand-edited triggarr.toml with a URL such as http://0.0.0.0:7878 (unspecified address; on Linux host networking this actually connects to the local host), a link-local 169.254.x.x literal, or a metadata hostname loaded without error. Now the load raises pydantic.ValidationError, and ensure_config deliberately lets that propagate uncaught (docstring at triggarr/config.py:345). The result is an unhandled traceback and, under Docker restart policies, a crash loop. The web settings form already rejected these values through the strict validate_arr_url (triggarr/web/routes.py:561), so the only configs affected are hand-edited TOML. This is a tightening that the D-01/D-02 docstring says is intended. 0.0.0.0 falls outside the documented URL contract (validate_arr_url's docstring blocks unspecified addresses), so the confidence cap applies. pending: confirm that no supported deployment pattern (e.g. Linux network_mode: host with http://0.0.0.0:PORT) is in use and documented. If one is, this is a startup regression for those users.
findings.title: New load-time URL validator can stop the daemon from starting if an existing config has a URL that was previously accepted
findings.why_it_matters: This is the first release where a config that loaded before can fail to load. It affects upgrading users with hand-edited TOML, and the failure is a raw traceback instead of the project's usual friendly exit.

findings.problem: When the new validator rejects a URL at startup, the uncaught pydantic.ValidationError's string form includes input_value='<url>'. A URL with userinfo credentials (http://user:pass@169.254.x.x) would then be printed in the traceback. The settings-POST path logs the same exc through loguru (routes.py:599-600), so the existing redacting sink may or may not scrub it. The pre-existing reject_apikey_in_url validator has the same shape, so this diff widens an existing exposure rather than creating a new one. pending: show that an uncaught startup ValidationError bypasses the redacting sink and that userinfo URLs are a realistic input.
findings.title: Startup ValidationError output includes the raw URL as input_value, which is not passed through the loguru redacting sink
